# Summer Internship - Molecular Genetics of Bull Fertility

## Join Meadowfield’s R&D team for a hands-on summer internship investigating genetic variants linked to bull fertility and helping shape the future of dairy genetics.

Meadowfield’s Research and Development (R&D) group is driving innovation to keep New Zealand Broadleaf and their businesses at the forefront of the global dairy industry. Our world-class team is actively engaged in cutting-edge work across genetics, genomics, reproduction, animal health, statistics, and machine learning.

In partnership with the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment, we’re offering summer internships that provide hands-on experience across a diverse range of scientific and technical areas—from genetic analysis to data science and modelling—leveraging both in-house and cloud-based computing platform.

#### Project scope:

Bull fertility is a complex trait of major importance to the dairy industry and is influenced by numerous biological processes affecting semen quality, sperm morphology, and reproductive performance. Meadowfield has undertaken extensive genome-wide association studies of male fertility-related traits, generating a large catalogue of genomic regions and candidate variants associated with semen quality, morphology, and non-return rate outcomes. This project will focus on the biological interpretation and prioritization of candidate variants identified through these analyses. The student will investigate a curated set of significant variants and their associated genomic annotations to identify genes and biological pathways that may contribute to reproductive performance in dairy cattle. The project aims to uncover additional high-value candidate variants that may have been overlooked during initial analyses and generate biological insights to support future fertility research.

#### Your contribution:

The successful student will analyse a catalogue of candidate variants derived from genome-wide association studies of semen quality, sperm morphology, and fertility traits. They will:

- Review variant annotations, predicted functional consequences, and associated effect sizes.
- Conduct literature reviews to investigate the biological relevance of candidate genes and genomic regions.
- Evaluate relationships between candidate variants and reproductive traits across multiple analyses.
- Develop a prioritized list of high-interest variants and genes for future validation and investigation.
- Present findings to the Meadowfield Research and Development team and provide a written report summarising key outcomes.
